newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon mortars wound one Israeli soldier.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon mortars wound one Israeli soldier.

text.p: An Israeli army commander said on Friday Lebanon's Hizbollah guerrillas fired mortar bombs into northern Israel in violation of a year-old ceasefire understanding.
Israel's northern area commander Major-General Amiram Levine said one Israeli soldier was wounded in the firing.

Sources from the South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia, which patrols a strip in south Lebanon along with Israeli troops, had said guerrillas fired three salvoes of Katyusha rockets into a number of pro-Israeli SLA outposts inside the occupation zone.
Levine said that mortars hit Israeli outposts on the borders and an area inside Israel, in breach of an April 26 Lebanon ceasefire understanding banning Hizbollah from firing into northern Israel.
"Before six o'clock Hizbollah shot 120 mm mortars at two of our positions, including at an area in Israel," he told reporters inside the occupation zone.
"Hizbollah must understand that it's against the agreement of understandings because they shot into an area of Israel which under no circumstances are they allowed to do," he added.

In Beirut, Hizbollah said its guerrillas fired three salvoes of Katyusha rockets into the border outposts in response to Israeli "aggressions against Lebanese civilians, the last of which were in Kfar Tibneet."

On Thursday, a Lebanese policeman and a civilian were wounded when Israeli and SLA gunmen opened machinegun fire at the crossing point of Kfar Tibneet, on the edge of the zone, Lebanese security sources said. They said a bullet hit a third civilian in the leg at his house in Kfar Tibneet.
Levine said Hizbollah also fired five or six Katyusha rockets at an SLA position near the SLA-held town of Marjayoun.
Friday's incident brought to 27 the number of Israeli soldiers wounded in guerrilla attacks in south Lebanon since the beginning of the year. Six soldiers have been killed over the same period.
Hizbollah guerrillas attack the Israeli soldiers and their SLA allies in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine-mile) south Lebanon occupation zone.
